title: Fair and Interpretable Models for Survival Analysis

problem.claim: Survival analysis predicts event risk under censoring, but existing survival techniques can produce unintended bias toward protected attributes.

gap.claim: Common censoring assumptions are often violated in real data, which can cause overestimation and biased survival predictions across protected groups.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces fairness definitions based on survival functions and censoring.
The paper proposes fair and interpretable survival models using pseudo-value-based objective functions with fairness constraints to predict subject-specific survival probabilities.
The paper studies the interplay between interpretability and fairness and examines how fairness and censoring affect survival predictions for different protected attributes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their fairness definitions and survival models as introduced or novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world survival datasets are reported to show significant improvement over existing survival techniques in accuracy and fairness measures.
The authors report fair predictions for protected attributes under different types and amounts of censoring.

narrative_sequence.summary: Survival analysis predicts event risk in the presence of censoring.
Existing survival techniques may exhibit unintended bias toward protected attributes.
The paper introduces fairness definitions based on survival functions and censoring.
The paper proposes fair and interpretable survival models with pseudo-value-based objectives and fairness constraints.
The authors report improvements on three real-world datasets and analyze fairness, interpretability, and censoring effects.

source_observation.claim: Censoring assumptions that are violated in real data can contribute to biased predictions across protected groups.

interpretation.claim: Fairness analysis in survival modeling should account for censoring mechanisms rather than treating censoring as unrelated to prognosis and covariates.

application.claim: When developing group-sensitive survival models, define fairness criteria with explicit reference to survival functions and censoring.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these fairness definitions or models generalize beyond the reported settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, dataset sizes, protected attributes, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the exact fairness definitions, model architecture, pseudo-value construction, or constraint formulation.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, baselines, statistical tests, or implementation details.
